question: What defines a normal labour in terms of fetal presentation?
explanation: Normal labour requires the fetus to present head-first, known as a cephalic presentation, to allow smooth passage through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: A woman at term delivers vaginally without instruments or complications. How is this labour classified?
explanation: Eutocia is the medical term for normal, uncomplicated vaginal labour and delivery at term. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: What is the primary driving force behind the mechanism of labour?
explanation: Rhythmic uterine contractions provide the primary expulsive power that pushes the fetus through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: Why does the fetal head perform specific positional movements during birth?

options.A: To protect the umbilical cord from compression
options.B: To adapt to the changing diameters of the pelvis
options.C: To position the placenta for immediate delivery
options.D: To stimulate cervical dilatation and effacement

explanation: The fetus must navigate the narrow and angled bony pelvis by rotating and flexing to match the available space. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: What fetal landmark passing the pelvic inlet signifies engagement?
explanation: Engagement is confirmed when the biparietal diameter, the widest transverse measurement of the fetal head, passes the pelvic inlet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: When does engagement typically happen in a first-time mother (primigravida)?

options.A: A few weeks before labour starts
options.B: Only during the second stage of labour
options.C: During the third stage of placental delivery
options.D: Immediately after the rupture of membranes

explanation: First-time mothers usually experience fetal head engagement late in the third trimester, prior to the onset of actual labour contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: What anatomical part of the fetus touches the chest during head flexion?
explanation: Flexion forces the fetal chin to tuck tightly against the chest, reducing the presenting diameter of the head. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: Why is flexion of the fetal head critical during normal labour?

options.A: It presents a smaller head diameter to the birth canal
options.B: It accelerates the dilation of an oedematous cervix
options.C: It prevents premature rupture of the amniotic membranes
options.D: It rotates the occiput toward the maternal sacrum

explanation: Tucking the chin exchanges a wide skull diameter for a narrow suboccipitobregmatic diameter, easing passage through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: Where does the fetal occiput usually rotate to during internal rotation?

options.C: Obliquely into the left sacroiliac joint

explanation: Internal rotation typically brings the fetal occiput to the front, resting directly under the maternal pubic symphysis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: What anatomical structure in the pelvis forces the fetal head to rotate internally?
explanation: The gutter-shaped pelvic floor muscles slope downwards and forwards, guiding the leading part of the head to rotate anteriorly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: What part of the maternal pelvis acts as a fulcrum during fetal head extension?
explanation: The lower border of the pubic symphysis serves as a pivot point around which the fetal head extends upward. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: What physical forces cause the fetal head to extend after internal rotation?

options.A: Relaxation of the maternal abdominal wall
options.B: Uterine thrust and pelvic floor resistance
options.C: Manual traction applied by the midwife
options.D: Gravitational pull on the fetal shoulders

explanation: Contractions push the baby down while the perineum pushes up, forcing the head to pivot outward in extension. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: What movement immediately follows the birth of the fetal head?
explanation: Restitution is the immediate, spontaneous untwisting of the neck that realigns the head with the shoulders. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)

question: Why does external rotation of the fetal head occur outside the vagina?

options.A: The mother is actively twisting the baby's neck
options.B: The umbilical cord wraps tightly around the shoulders
options.C: The shoulders are rotating internally inside the pelvis
options.D: Gravity pulls unevenly on the heavy fetal cranium

explanation: As the shoulders turn inside the pelvis to fit the outlet, the visible head outside mimics that movement through external rotation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)

question: Which fetal part is delivered first during the birth of the shoulders?
explanation: The anterior shoulder emerges first from beneath the pubic symphysis before the posterior shoulder is delivered. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h8)

question: How do the shoulders clear the perineum during final expulsion?

options.A: By direct axial traction from the birth attendant
options.B: By forceful maternal pushing against a closed glottis
options.C: By lateral flexion of the fetal spine
options.D: By rotational pivoting around the coccyx tip

explanation: The body bends sideways laterally to allow the shoulders to sweep over the perineum without tearing tissues. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h8)
